title: Mentorship & Student Research
text:
As Director of Public Health Research at Morehouse School of Medicine (MSM),
Dr. Gemechu B. Gerbi has made mentorship a cornerstone of his academic career.
He works closely with students to design rigorous research questions, apply
epidemiologic and biostatistical methods, interpret national surveillance data,
and present actionable findings to improve population health.
His work prioritizes health disparities and equity, ensuring students confront
real-world public health challenges and contribute to solutions that matter.



– 100+ student-led research presentations at APHA, AACR, RCMI, MSM Research Symposiums, and national health disparities conferences.
– Mentorship producing peer-reviewed manuscripts and first-author student publications.
– Leadership of MPH research initiatives advancing careers in: - Public health analytics - Applied epidemiology - Cancer prevention - Chronic disease equity - Behavioral and mental health research

“Dr. Gerbi supports students in transforming data into impact.”






Cancer screening among underrepresented populations

Chronic disease burden (heart disease, COPD, stroke)

Adolescent mental health and violence exposure

Sexual and reproductive health (HPV, PID, HIV)

Health-related behaviors & quality of life

Youth risk behaviors using YRBSS

Maternal & child health disparities

All rooted in national datasets, including BRFSS, NSFG, and NHANES.




Each bullet below represents students trained and co-authored by Dr. Gerbi:

Sociodemographic Disparities in Breast Cancer Screening — Cancer Research Symposium (2025)

Determinants of Depression Among Adults in the U.S. — Xavier Health Disparities Conference (2023)

Low Birth Weight Inequities in the U.S. — APHA Annual Meeting (2023)

Bullying, Mental Distress & Suicide Risk in Adolescents — APHA Annual Meeting (2023)

Predictors of Heart Attack in U.S. Adults — MSM Research Symposium (2020)

These represent just a few of dozens of student-driven projects in which he has provided: ✔ methodological guidance
✔ data analysis mentorship
✔ abstract and manuscript development support





“Public health research is not only about data — it is about shaping leaders
who know how to use evidence to transform communities.”

Dr. Gerbi cultivates: - Independence in analytical decision-making
- Clarity in scientific communication
- Confidence in professional presentation
- Commitment to community impact




Students in the MPH program interested in:
✔ BRFSS / NSFG / NHANES analysis
✔ SAS or SPSS data analytics training
✔ Conference presentations & manuscript writing
…may inquire about current research opportunities.
📧 Contact: ggerbi@msm.edu

Dr. Gerbi is proud of every student who discovers their voice, gains
new skills, and contributes meaningfully to public health knowledge.

Research mentorship is not an add-on — it’s his mission.

title: Current Projects
text:
Dr. Gerbi’s current work focuses on three complementary streams.

Epidemiology and Health Data Science
First, he is developing an Epidemiology & Health Data Science concentration that integrates machine learning, bioinformatics, and public health informatics to prepare students for modern analytic practice.
Website forthcoming


Student Projects
Second, he leads and mentors MPH students on population health and cancer prevention studies that interrogate screening disparities and social determinants using large national datasets, as reflected in recent presentations on breast, cervical, and colorectal cancer screening.


Research Core at MSM’s DPHE
Third, building on his EIS foundations in surveillance and outbreak response, he continues to bridge research, practice, and policy with community-centered projects focused on health equity.

title: Welcome
text:
Dr. Gemechu B. Gerbi is a Professor of Epidemiology and Biostatistics and Director of Public Health Research at Morehouse School of Medicine. With more than two decades of experience spanning academic leadership, applied epidemiology, and community-focused scholarship, his work advances health equity through rigorous research, transformative teaching, and mentorship. His practice foundations include service as an Epidemic Intelligence Service (EIS) Officer at the U.S. CDC, where he led field investigations such as the 2012–2013 hepatitis E outbreak among refugees in South Sudan. His research spans social determinants of health, HIV/AIDS prevention, chronic disease epidemiology, computational modeling of infectious diseases, and mental health—primarily in underserved communities.
A prolific educator and mentor, Dr. Gerbi has directed the epidemiology, biostatistics, and research methods core curriculum for more than a decade and is currently pioneering an Epidemiology & Health Data Science concentration that integrates machine learning, bioinformatics, and public health informatics. He has authored over 40 peer-reviewed publications, two book chapters, and more than 120 presentations and published abstracts at national and international conferences.

title: Resume
text: Dr. Gerbi’s career centers on advancing population health through teaching, scholarship, and service. He currently serves as Professor of Epidemiology and Biostatistics and Director of Public Health Research in the Master of Public Health Program at Morehouse School of Medicine, roles he has held while progressing from Assistant to Associate to full Professor since 2014.

title: Resume
text:
Education
He earned a PhD in Integrative Biosciences/Epidemiology and an MSc in Epidemiology/Veterinary Science from Tuskegee University, and a BA in Sociology from Addis Ababa University. His doctoral dissertation focused on HIV/AIDS in Alabama’s Black Belt Counties.

title: Resume
text:
Practice Foundations
He completed the CDC’s Epidemic Intelligence Service (EIS) training as an officer in the Division of Viral Hepatitis, strengthening expertise in surveillance, outbreak response, and program evaluation.

title: Resume
text:
Teaching Leadership
At Morehouse School of Medicine, he has directed core MPH courses in Epidemiology, Biostatistics, and Research Methods, with additional roles across global health systems and online modalities.

title: Resume
text:
Academic Service & Leadership
He directs Public Health Research for the MPH Program and serves on admissions, progress, and graduate education committees; he is also a site visitor for the Council on Education for Public Health and has held national service roles including editorial advisory work for APHA’s The Nation’s Health.

title: Resume
text:
Recognition
Honors include Outstanding Mentor, Distinguished Teaching, Best Embodies MSM Mission, and multiple Outstanding Advisor awards, reflecting sustained excellence in mentorship and pedagogy.
